ashby:airwallex:a139d336-cea8-4b73-b391-.summary:
Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own.

We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,700 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told…

sections.title: How you'll make impact
paras: Own the end-to-end delivery of complex Spend and corporate card implementations for enterprise and high-growth customers across the US, turning agreed business requirements and solution designs into actionable plans that land on time, on scope, and to a high quality bar.

Act as a trusted technical advisor across high-value implementations and expansions, shaping integration approaches, system configuration, solution design, and the use of ERP, HRIS, API, and third-party connector integrations. You’ll work closely with Sales, Merchant Services, Solutions Engineering, Product, Operations, Risk, activation and onboarding teams, account management, and external partners including networks, processors, and manufacturers.

Lead technical discovery, understand customer systems, data flows, and workflows, and guide customers through complex configuration decisions and integration hurdles. You’ll focus on robust, maintainable implementations rather than writing code directly, while serving as a subject matter expert on the wider integration ecosystem.

sections.title: Essentials
bullets: A bachelor’s degree in a related field such as Business, Finance, Engineering, or Information Systems, or equivalent practical experience.
5+ years of experience in implementation, onboarding, customer success, or project or program management, managing complex, multi-stakeholder technology or financial services implementations.
4+ years of client-facing delivery or professional services experience in a fast-paced environment such as SaaS, fintech, consulting, systems integration, or enterprise implementation.
A track record of successfully delivering cross-functional projects with stakeholders from diverse backgrounds and job functions, including C-level executives, technical teams, and operations.
Exceptional written and verbal communication and presentation skills, including the ability to lead steering meetings, write clear status updates, and influence decisions without direct authority.

Experience delivering ERP, accounting system, or expense platform implementations, such as NetSuite, SAP, Oracle, or Xero, including associated data flows such as GL, cost centres, entities, and card feeds.

sections.title: Preferred
bullets: Hands-on experience working with or alongside integration engineers, solution architects, or technical program managers on API-based integrations, including familiarity with common web, SSO, and ERP integration concepts.

Formal training or certification in project management or agile delivery, such as PMP, PRINCE2, or Scrum Master, and comfort setting up operating rhythms such as stand-ups, steering committees, and executive readouts.
Experience managing strategic or enterprise accounts as part of a broader account team, including navigating commercial sensitivities while protecting delivery quality and scope.
The ability to thrive in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment, balancing structured methodologies with pragmatic decision-making to keep complex projects moving forward.

sections.title: You'll thrive here if
bullets: You’re comfortable with ambiguity. Give you a problem, not a prescription, and you’ll run with it.
You connect dots across functions and hold the big picture without losing grip on the details.
You simplify complexity rather than hiding behind it.
You over-communicate by design. You’d rather flag something early than let it become a surprise.
You know when to align and when to just decide. Collaboration isn’t a way to avoid accountability.

ashby:alternativepayments:776979ef-0a1e-.summary:
Alternative Payments is building the financial operating system for SMBs, consolidating the disconnected tech stack that holds service-based businesses back. Starting with MSPs, we've spent five years perfecting accounts receivable, and we're now expanding into accounts payable, AI-powered analytics with Alti, and beyond. We're at an inflection point: closing the loop on money movement and laying the foundation for a platform that will reshape how service businesses operate financially.

We're growing fast, thinking big, and building a global team that wants to be part of something that lasts. If you're energized by real problems, real customers, and real impact, we want to hear from you.

sections.title: A note from Baxter, our founder and CEO
paras: When I started Alternative Payments, I wanted to build the kind of place I never got to work at before: somewhere people grow, take real ownership, and do the best work of their careers. Five years in, that’s still the goal, and this role is a big part of it.

We started by helping MSPs get paid. Today more than 1,000 service businesses trust us with how money moves through their business, and we’ve grown from receivables into payables, analytics and Alti, our financial AI. The most important work in finance is shifting to agentic workflows, and we intend to lead that shift for service businesses.

That’s why this hire matters so much. You won’t be maintaining a roadmap someone else wrote. You’ll own a product area, figure out what our customers need before they can name it, and ship the first version of products that don’t exist yet. What you build will shape what Alternative Payments becomes.

sections.title: What we're looking for
paras: We're hiring a Senior Product Manager to build new products that are strategic bets for our platform from ideation to launch. You'll join a small product team where each PM owns an area (today: accounts receivable, accounts payable, and Alti) and work directly with our CEO and an engineering team that builds with AI.

sections.title: What you'll do
bullets: Turn loosely defined business goals into a clear problem statement, a sequenced plan, and a written case that leadership and engineering can act on.
Prioritize product roadmap, decide which problems in your area to solve, using customer conversations, data, support volume and competitive research, and defend that order.
Take new products from 0 to 1: discovery, scoping, launch and adoption.
Set success and guardrail metrics before work begins, and stop work that isn't earning its place, including work already in flight.
Own the full launch: enablement for sales, CX and support, pricing implications, and rollout.
Write PRDs engineering can build from without a follow-up meeting, engage on design docs and tradeoffs, and use multiple AI tools in your daily work.
Help shape the shared PM process our team is building, so discovery, prioritization and documentation work the same way across product areas.

sections.title: What you'll bring
bullets: 5+ years of product management in B2B, including at least one product you took from 0 to 1 and launched to customers.
Experience in payments, money movement or finance operations, or in another complex B2B domain such as multi-product software for SMB or mid-market businesses.
Structured problem-solving: you ask questions before giving opinions, and you can break an ambiguous ask into a plan with a clear first step.
A strong sense of ownership, holding yourself accountable for outcomes across team boundaries and resolving cross-functional friction directly.
Coachability that shows up as genuinely changing your position on something you'd publicly committed to when the evidence calls for it.
The ability to reach working expertise in an unfamiliar domain fast enough to be useful in it quickly, rather than waiting to be fully briefed.
Clear writing, and the ability to defend a prioritization with data.
Comfort making calls with incomplete information, and changing course when the evidence changes.

We're looking for a GTM Enablement Manager who enjoys translating technical concepts into language the field can use with confidence — someone who's as comfortable in a room with engineers as they are building the materials an AE needs to navigate a tricky customer conversation. This is a builder role — you'll own the strategy, content, and delivery that get our field (AEs, SEs, and CSMs) equipped to sell and support Apollo's current customers and future customers.

sections.title: Overview
paras: Reporting to the Head of Sales, you'll partner closely with Product, Engineering, Product Marketing, and Field leadership — so the work you do shows up directly in how fast the team ramps and how well we retain customers.

sections.title: What you'll do
bullets: Design and own our enablement strategy end-to-end, building role-based learning paths for AEs, SEs, and CSMs across self-directed learning, just-in-time delivery, micro-learning, and major learning events.

Partner with RevOps to define field productivity baselines and the leading indicators — ramp time, certification engagement, time-to-first-value — that connect enablement work to business outcomes, and track whether training is actually landing over time.

Act as the connective tissue between engineering and the field, translating what's shipping and why it matters into language non-technical AEs and CSMs can use with confidence in front of customers.
Deliver training that actually lands — not just build the content, but leading the sessions, measuring impact and effectiveness, and adjusting as needed.

Bring AI into how the field works, using it to speed up content creation, mine tools like Gong for field insights, and track how reps are positioning Apollo with customers — while coaching AEs and CSMs on how to use AI in their own workflows.
Drive alignment across teams that don't report to you, pulling input and buy-in from Product, Engineering, Marketing, and Field leadership to get assets built and adopted.

sections.title: Who you are

A proven track record of live delivery — not just content creation. You can teach a technical concept to a non-technical audience, read whether it's landing in real time, and adjust.
Demonstrated ownership in ambiguous environments: you've built something from scratch before, set your own priorities, and been accountable for the result.
Strong cross-functional influence skills: you've driven alignment and gotten things built by pulling in people who don't report to you.
Practical, hands-on AI fluency, not just familiarity — you've used AI as a force multiplier to get more out of your own work, and you can teach non-technical teammates to do the same.

ashby:code-metal:fc471444-dfef-43df-95a8.summary: Code Metal is the leader in automated software engineering you can trust. As AI writes more of the world's code, the bottleneck in software has shifted from writing code to verifying it works, and AI cannot verify its own work with certainty. Code Metal takes a fundamentally different approach: constrain AI to what it does reliably, verify every step independently of the model using formal methods, and keep engineers in the loop on the decisions that matter. The result isn't code that probably works — it's code that is provably correct, with auditable proof. Customers including the U.S. Air Force, L3Harris, RTX, and Toshiba use Code Metal to modernize legacy code, optimize performance on real hardware, and move prototypes to production, fast. Founded in 2023 with offices in Boston and San Francisco, Code Metal is funded by Accel, Salesforce Ventures, B Capital, Smith Point Capital, J2…

sections.title: Solutions Engineer
paras: Code Metal is looking for a Solutions Engineer to sit at the intersection of engineering, prototyping, and customer growth - turning promising opportunities into working technical systems. You'll be a hands-on bridge between our platform and real-world use, building and validating customer solutions through proofs of concept and early development, then helping transition successful work toward repeatable production use.

sections.title: Who thrives in this role:
bullets: Engineers who enjoy turning loosely defined customer problems into working systems.
Technically curious people who can quickly explore unfamiliar domains, prototype approaches, and turn what they learn into working solutions.
Hands-on builders who combine strong technical judgment with rapid execution and follow-through.
Comfortable owning the technical execution of a customer problem - from a scoped opportunity through a validated proof of concept and early deployment.
Thrive in open-ended environments and can context-switch quickly across technical domains.
Willing to learn quickly and go deep when a customer problem demands it.

A strong technical background is required, whether your experience comes from engineering, research, or other technical roles. You'll often be among the first engineers to prove how Code Metal's technology can solve a new customer problem in practice.

sections.title: Responsibilities:
bullets: Turn scoped customer opportunities into working technical solutions that demonstrate how Code Metal's technology can be applied in real-world systems.
Work with customer engineers and stakeholders to understand development needs, system constraints, and success criteria, then translate them into executable implementation plans.
Rapidly investigate unfamiliar technical domains and de-risk solution paths through hands-on prototyping, integration, and feasibility testing.
Build and lead proofs of concept (PoCs), working with Solutions Architects, product, engineering, and customer teams to turn an agreed approach into a validated system.
Implement complex algorithms and compute-heavy pipelines (DSP, RF, communications, and similar workloads) on GPUs, FPGAs, and edge systems using Code Metal's platform.
Profile, debug, and tune PoCs and early deployments for latency, throughput, memory, and power across heterogeneous compute environments.
Debug across heterogeneous systems (CPU/GPU/FPGA), identifying and resolving issues spanning algorithms, software, hardware, and toolchains.
Use PoCs and technical demos to make Code Metal's product differentiators concrete and measurable for customers.

sections.title: Requirements:
bullets: Strong background in computer science, systems engineering, electrical engineering, physics, or a related technical field.

ashby:delinea:a3642937-f89b-45b8-bf2c-65.summary:

Delinea is the identity security platform that continuously controls what AI agents, humans and machines can do and for how long. It extends privileged access management from the point of access to the moment of action, using just-in-time authorization to reduce standing privilege across on-premises, multi-cloud and short-lived infrastructure, without adding friction for legitimate users. Dexmate is building the foundation for physical AI — combining a new generation of robots with a universal Physical AI OS, making robots as easy to build and deploy as software. Today, robotics is fragmented, slow, and closed: most builders are forced to reinvent the same stack again and again, and most ideas never make it past the prototype stage. We exist to change that. Hi, I'm Joe, Head of Customer Success at Whippy. I'm hiring an Associate Solutions Engineer to design and build the solutions our customers run their business on. This isn't a pre-sale demo role. After the deal closes, you own the customer: you scope their problem, build the workflows, AI agents, and integrations that solve it, and grow the account from there.

This role is built for someone early in their career (0-1 years of experience), and new grads are welcome. You'll ramp alongside me and experienced teammates, then take ownership of your own customers as you prove you're ready.

sections.title: Why I'm hiring
paras: At Whippy, we view Customer Success as a revenue engine, not a cost center, because if customers don't get value from a tool, they'll leave. Whippy has six incredible products today because we've always built alongside our customers. That's how we evolved from a simple texting platform to now powering calls, texts, email, AI agents, and complex messaging and business automations for over 1,000 businesses. We ship fast to meet our customers' needs.

Most customers start with one use case, like a staffing firm using an AI voice agent to screen candidates. They stay and grow because they see real ROI, then expand use cases until Whippy becomes the infrastructure their business runs on. Your job is to drive that growth: make their first outcome happen during onboarding and implementation, uncover the next problem, and help them get even more value.

In this role, you'll mainly work with customers in the staffing industry. Their data flows into Whippy from their ATS, most often TempWorks, Avionte, Aqore/Zenople, Crelate, or Bullhorn, so you'll learn how staffing firms recruit and place talent, and how to build on top of their data.

bullets: Design and build solutions in Whippy without engineering : workflows, AI voice and text agents, automations, and data syncs back into the customer's ATS.
Scope technical requirements with customers , translate them into a working build, and test and verify every piece before it goes live.
Own the customer after go-live , from onboarding through renewal and expansion, as their single point of contact and trusted technical advisor.
Learn fast. Shadow calls, get hands-on coaching from me, and take on more ownership every month.
Pick up the phone. Reach out proactively, ask the question instead of guessing, and get ahead of problems before they turn into escalations.
Own your gross and net revenue retention , and get rewarded for beating targets.
Tie usage to business outcomes , and report value back in the metrics customers actually care about.
Spot expansion signals and hand warm leads to sales when usage outgrows the contract.

sections.title: Our customer success values
paras: This is a high-performance environment, and I'll coach and support you through it. You'll be challenged, coached, and you'll always know where you stand. CS is a team sport, so it's okay to ask for help, experiment, fail, and pivot. A few things that are true here:
bullets: Everyone is a builder. Our team builds in the product without engineering, and the best product ideas come from you, the person closest to the customer. We use AI to move fast, but we own our work, verify every fact, and don't ship slop.
We lead with expertise, not order-taking. We get curious about the why behind every request, and we say no when no is the right answer.
We work like owners, not clock-watchers. We care about outcomes, not hours. We take initiative, pick up the phone, and work obsessively on the problem in front of us.
CS is a revenue engine, not a cost center. We treat it as the growth engine of the company and pay for results.

sections.title: What we're looking for
bullets: Communication above all. This is the number one predictor of success in this role. You overcommunicate by default with customers, your team, and me. You're clear in writing and on calls, you set expectations, and you never leave people guessing.
Fast and proactive. You process information quickly, ask for what you need instead of waiting, and show up to every call prepared.
Curious, coachable, and low-ego. You're a fast learner who wants feedback, digs into the why behind every request, and gets better quickly.
Comfortable getting technical. You don't need to code, but you're the kind of person who enjoys taking a tool apart, figuring out how it works, and building something useful with it.
Strategic and commercial. You see usage and growth, not just tickets, and you're comfortable owning a number and an upgrade conversation.

Self-directed. You take initiative, stay organized without being told, and run your own book without anyone managing your calendar. Calm under pressure.

0-1 years of experience , and new grads are welcome. paras: Backblaze is the object storage leader in the open cloud movement, fueling customer success with cloud storage built purposefully to unlock budgets, unburden administrators, and unleash innovators. Together with our partners, we're helping customers break free from the restrictive, overpriced legacy solutions that hold them back, and blaze forward with the full power of the open cloud in their hands.

We started by building storage servers from scratch in a Palo Alto apartment to save 90% on hardware. Turns out hard constraints make for pretty good engineering. That discipline forged a platform that performs as well or better than competitors, scales to multi-exabyte workloads, and costs a fraction of what AWS or Google charge. AI infrastructure runs on data. Storage gets hard at scale. We've been breaking, rebuilding, and improving that storage layer for 20 years.

paras: Reporting to the Director of Customer Programs, we need an operator to own enablement for a post-sales organization that is growing fast: Support, Customer Success, Customer Growth, Adoption and Flagship Account Management. You will work alongside the CX Enablement Specialist, who also reports to the Director and knows how Backblaze really works: the backend, customer provisioning, the core systems and Salesforce. The Specialist brings deep knowledge of how things work here, and you bring structure and learning design. Together you turn that knowledge into learning paths and training that every new hire can follow, and you shape how the two of you share the work.
You have built and run post-sales teams, you know how to turn chaos into a working system, and you bring a point of view on how a post-sales organization should be enabled at scale.

sections.title: Build
bullets: The post-sales enablement strategy and multi-quarter roadmap, tied to the 2027 plan and to the metrics each team is accountable for. You present it to the VP and post-sales leaders and adjust it as the business changes.
A clear read on where teams struggle, using scorecard data and conversations with leaders, and the judgment to decide which gaps to close first.
The enablement operating model: how enablement is requested, built, approved, updated and retired, the quality standard for all content, and who owns what.
Role-based learning paths, skill levels and a formal certification and badging framework, designed with the post-sales leaders, so each role has a clear way to progress and to prove readiness.

Formal onboarding for Customer Success managers and Support, where onboarding today is largely informal, then extended to Growth, Adoption and Flagship. You run it through the 2027 hiring wave so new hires reach productivity quickly and consistently.
The release-to-enablement process with Product: product releases and roadmap changes turned into training, talking points and resources for each role, ready before customers ask.
Readiness for major system and process changes, such as the Planhat rollout, the move from Zendesk to Salesforce and new handoffs between teams.

Playbooks and cross-team handoffs (Sales to Adoption, Adoption to Customer Success, Support to Enterprise Support), led with the team leaders who own them, and with SOPs and RevOps so we build on company-wide processes.

sections.title: Own
bullets: One enablement calendar for all post-sales teams, so leaders know what is coming and when.

The enablement scorecard: new-hire ramp time, onboarding completion, playbook adoption and the effect on team metrics such as CSAT, time to first value and retention. You review results quarterly with post-sales leadership and advise on decisions where enablement is a constraint, such as hiring pace and ramp expectations.

Your partnership with the CX Enablement Specialist, whose knowledge of how Backblaze works is the foundation of our training. You turn that expertise into structured, repeatable training and agree how to share the work.

sections.title: Unlocking AI Agents for the Finance Admin
paras: Companies buy Brex to run their spend, and the person on the hook for that is the finance admin — a controller, an accounting manager, a finance ops lead. Their job comes down to two things they can never quite get ahead of: making sure money is being spent compliantly and documented in time to close the books, and knowing where the company's money is actually going.

Today they do both by hand, at a scale that doesn't work. Roughly 4% of travel and entertainment spend is out of policy — for a company spending $10M a year, that's $400K in violations, duplicates, missing receipts, and overspend. Most companies never find it, because finding it means a human reading transactions one at a time. The ones who do find it either staff a review team or bolt on a separate audit product with its own login. On the other side, the questions that actually matter — where did spend grow this quarter, which team is drifting, what's driving the number — sit behind a queue for an analyst, or a spreadsheet the admin builds themselves at month-end. Nobody is continuously watching.
The AI team is working to give every finance admin two people they can't hire today: an auditor and a business analyst.

From there you go as deep as it takes to make it real: shaping agent behavior, writing and iterating prompts, designing the evals that prove it works, and digging into traces when it doesn't. greenhouse:faire:8934059002.summary: Faire is a technology wholesale platform built on the belief that the future is local. Independent retailers around the globe collectively represent a multi-hundred-billion-dollar wholesale market that has historically been fragmented and offline. At Faire, we're using the power of tech, data, and machine learning to connect this thriving community of entrepreneurs across the globe. Picture your favorite boutique in town — we help them discover the best products from around the world to sell in their stores. With the right tools and insights, we believe that we can level the playing field so businesses can grow and local communities can thrive.

sections.title: About this role
paras: You’ll own making sure all brands can succeed on Faire, whether they are just starting out or driving millions a year. Faire has a robust suite of programs and tools that help brands grow, and when brands take our guidance, they grow measurably faster - driving top actions is worth an estimated 15-30% increase in brand lifetime value. The catch is that today, most guidance comes from calls with account managers, and brands have no reliable way to discover or act on it themselves: our notifications, nudges, and emails deliver disjointed advice, don’t give sufficient context, and aren’t personalized to what matters most for a given brand’s shop setup and goals.

Your job is to build a system that can score a brand’s shop, measure the value of potential actions, identify the top opportunities, and communicate those to our brands at the right time and in a compelling way. You’ll work closely with the pods that built the programs to deeply understand the mechanics and the adoption blockers, and with our Success, Product Marketing, and Sales teams to deliver an omnichannel strategy for driving adoption.

If you love figuring out what makes users successful, building systems that change behavior, working across product and GTM teams, and you get excited about creating real, measurable value for small business owners, this is the role for you.

sections.title: What you'll do
bullets: Set the strategy for brand success. Deeply understand which behaviors make brands successful on Faire, what blocks brands from adopting them, and where guidance should come from product versus a person.
Own the brand success roadmap end-to-end. Define strategy and sequencing across rebuilding key systems, shipping contextual nudges, and deep-diving into top actions.

Go deep on the highest-value actions. Understand blockers, build education and reasons to believe, determine contextual moments to target, and make each action as close to one click as possible, starting with what new brands need in their first 30 days.

Build the targeting and triggering system. Estimate the LTV impact of each action, rank each brand's personalized top opportunities, and fire on the behavioral moments when a brand is most likely to act.

Own the growth hub and rationalize our nudge systems. Give brands a single place to see what is limiting their growth and their top actions, and consolidate today's banners, emails and in-portal prompts into one prioritized system that other pods contribute to.

sections.title: Qualifications
bullets: Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.
You have 8+ years of experience in product at a high-growth tech startup, as a startup founder, or in a top tech company.
You have set direction in an ambiguous space, not just executed a roadmap you inherited. You can decide what's worth working on and explain why.
You are good at deeply understanding customer needs and underlying motivations, especially in spaces where customers aren't great at predicting how changes will impact their behavior.
You work well across teams. You've aligned other product teams and go-to-market partners on shared systems.
You are analytically rigorous. You define the right metrics, design experiments, and know the difference between adoption you caused and adoption that would have happened anyway.
You're an inspiring leader who is excited about the day-to-day of understanding our customers and working with a strong team to build improvements for them.
You're an extraordinarily fast learner. You have the natural curiosity and intellectual horsepower to deeply understand new topics and pick up new skills in a very short time.

sections.title: From the job description
paras: Most companies are adding AI to the software their teams already use. We're building it the other way around.

At Jetson, AI agents already do real operations work. They check rebate paperwork, plan the next steps on a project and draft replies to customers. People review that work, approve it and correct it, and every correction makes the agents better.
That changes the product question. It's no longer "what screen does this team need?" It's "which work should an agent do, which should a person do, and how do they hand it off?"

You'll own that answer for the people doing the work. Your customers are Jetson's own operations teams: rebates, project coordination, system design, customer success, billing, technical service and field operations. Each of them is moving onto one shared platform where people and agents work the same queue. You'll decide what each team sees, what the agents propose, what people approve, and how we know it's working.
bullets: Bring operations teams onto the platform, one at a time. Sit with a team, map how their work really runs, decide what goes in their first release, and get it adopted. Rebates and project coordination come first.
Design how people and agents share the work. For each type of task, decide whether an agent suggests it, a person approves it, or it runs on its own. Define what "done" means and what proof shows it.

Graduate work to autonomy with evidence. Every new agent action starts as a suggestion. When people accept it nearly every time, it moves to one-click approval, then to fully automatic. You set the bar and track whether each action has earned the next step.
Turn corrections into data. When someone rejects or edits an agent's work, that's a labelled example. Build the eval sets that catch a regression before it ships.
Read the trace. When an agent gets something wrong, open the trace and find out why: bad data, a missing rule, the wrong tool or a weak prompt. Fix the cause, not the symptom.
Experience: 5+ years as a product manager, shipping software people use every day. You care as much about how it feels to use as whether it works.

You've built with AI, not just used it. You've shipped something with a model inside it, even a side project, and you can tell us where it broke and what you did about it. You're comfortable in Claude Code or Cursor, SQL and Git.
You think in evals. "It works" isn't a claim until there's a set of real examples it passes. You'd rather show a precision number than a demo.

bullets: Redesign how Security is packaged and priced on Serverless. Define the tiers, feature entitlements, and usage meters, select what is bundled, metered, or sold as an add-on, test the options against customer demand and COGS, and bring a recommendation to senior executive team.

Own margin. Work with the Platform team and Finance to model the cost of new security capabilities, including ingest, search, retention, endpoint, and AI features, and set pricing requirements before a feature ships.

Grow Security on Serverless from proof of concept to renewal. You are accountable for new workloads, migrations from hosted and self-managed deployments, expansion, and retention. Work with Finance to separate recurring growth from one-time proof-of-concept revenue.

Give customers control over cost and performance. Define how search configurations, data tiers, and retention work for security use cases, and bring the cost models that justify new platform levers. Keep tenant-level packaging consistent with the Product Manager for MSSP and multi-tenancy.

Simplify how customers understand cost. Cut packaging complexity first, then simplify the sizing and pricing estimators that customers and Solutions Architects use. Agree on a measure of "simple," such as time to a credible quote, and track it.

Turn pricing decisions into shipped product. Write the PRDs and PRFAQs, and lead the work across Security engineering, the Serverless Platform team, Billing and Metering, and Cloud Operations. Help build the frameworks and reviews that other Security PMs, Product Marketing, and Solutions Architects use to price new capabilities.

Stay close to the market and the field. Discuss with customers and prospects about what they will and won't pay for, track how other security platforms package and price, and help the field explain when Serverless, hosted, or self-managed is the right fit.
You know the main approaches to pricing AI features, such as token-based, credit-based, and per-action or outcome pricing, and how inference costs and unpredictable usage shape each one.

Deals are how the largest buyers and sellers on the open internet do business with each other at The Trade Desk. What You'll Do

As a Staff Product Manager, you will set product direction for deal packaging, merchandising, and supply integration, and carry it from strategy through delivery and adoption. This is a senior individual contributor role with influence across the organization and across the industry.
